### Playbook: verify-fail-post-merge

- **Signal**: `{picked: <id>, approve: {blocked, reason: "verify-fail-post-merge"}}` — the post-merge verify genuinely ran and failed (`timedOut` is absent or `false`); the merge was rolled back and the target is unchanged.
- **What the machine tries**: Walk `docs/how-to/diagnose-a-verify-fail-post-merge-block-on-approve.md`'s steps directly, in this same session:
  1. Read `approve`'s own `output` field from the response (the full test-suite output, not just the recorded `verify` command) and identify exactly which test(s) failed.
  2. Check whether the failing test's file is inside the item's own diff (`fgos review <id>` or branch's changed files) — a failure in a file the item never touched is the first signal it's unrelated noise.
  3. Re-run the failing test file alone a few times (`node --test path/to/the-failing.test.mjs`) — reproduces deterministically (a genuine pre-existing bug) or only fails under full-suite run (load-induced flake).

The unit / workflow run schema has no field for a proof tier, `FULL_TRIGGERS`, or an environment fingerprint, and `disposition`/`rationale` accepts any non-empty string regardless of what it claims. A driver who does not actually run `FULL_TEST`, or who mislabels a real regression as `environmental-precondition`, is not caught by anything the runner checks -- this section is entirely Lead discipline in prose, not an enforced gate.

## 3. Independent Verification of Doer Commit and Tests

The driver must never accept worker self-narration, conversational claims, or ungrounded status reports:

1. **Verify Real Commit:** Directly inspect git history in the worktree (`git -C "$wt" log -1 --stat`) to verify substantive changes were committed.
2. **Verify Clean Tree:** Verify `git -C "$wt" status --porcelain` is clean (all worker edits committed).

authorAddedReferences.passage: | p-2a39f940 | Neither fgOS trigger path (interactive pick, headless runner) reaches an MVP2-equivalent outcome on its own terms — different failure shapes, not equivalent | Case 1 (interactive /fgOS:pick, tsk-57u, docs/history/mvp2-scope-test-infra/reports/case-1-interactive.md) reaches all three literal artifacts -- green verify (23 pass/0 fail), a real commit (4f501f1) on the item's own fgw/tsk-57u branch, and a clean worktree teardown -- but fgos return's fresh-claim path measures only the ORIGINAL checkout's HEAD, never the fgw/<id> branch pick itself created, so return structurally refuses to register the completed work and the item is stuck at awaiting-human instead of proposed/done. Case 2 (headless fgos-runner --once, docs/history/mvp2-scope-test-infra/reports/case-2-headless.md) never reaches ANY of the three artifacts: fgos-runner.mjs resolves repoRoot via git rev-parse --show-toplevel with no override flag/env, dogfood-fixture is not its own git repo, so a real --once invocation would claim and dispatch real forgent work off the live repo/.fgos/state.json (8 real items) -- confirmed unsafe twice, never invoked for real. Fix scope: (a) fgos return's branch-aware path (bin/fgos.mjs:1306) must also accept a first, ordinary interactive pick's fgw/<id> branch, not only a re-claimed already-blocked item's branchHeadAtTake; (b) fgos-runner needs a cwd-rooted root override (e.g. --root/FGOS_ROOT) parallel to the fgos.mjs verbs' existing process.cwd()-derived isolation, so the headless trigger can be pointed at a testbed instead of always resolving through git toplevel. Done when both cases can independently reach green verify + commit on own branch + clean teardown AND the engine registers completion (proposed/done), proven by re-running this feature's two live cases. | proposed | mvp2-scope-test-infra |

authorAddedReferences.passage: - [STR94] **`pnpm add -g github:vantt/forgent` fails: `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED`** (renumbered from STR88 -- ID collision found at merge time: main's own STR88, from a separate unpushed session, is an unrelated fgOS-plugin verb-wrapper feature. Feature slug `str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle` in `docs/history/` and bee decisions is unchanged, internal-only.) (ghi nhận 2026-07-23 từ friction `.bee/backlog.jsonl`, layer `install`, người dùng báo lỗi thật + đồng chốt root cause với một phiên agent khác) — `package.json`'s `scripts.prepare` chạy `node scripts/install-git-hooks.mjs`; script này đã no-op an toàn khi không có thư mục git metadata (`repo/scripts/install-git-hooks.mjs:8-20`, đã xác nhận đúng) — **lỗi không nằm ở logic script**. pnpm 10+ (qua `allowBuilds`) chặn CHẠY bất kỳ lifecycle script nào của một git-hosted dependency trước khi chạy nó, bất kể script đó làm gì — nên mọi user dùng `pnpm add -g github:vantt/forgent` đều dính `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED`, phải tự sửa `allowBuilds` trong `pnpm-workspace.yaml` mới cài được. Tái diễn với MỌI lần cài qua pnpm, không phải lỗi môi trường một lần; nhiều khả năng cũng ảnh hưởng các package manager strict khác (vd yarn PnP sau này) theo cùng cơ chế. **Fix đề xuất (đã thống nhất, per `str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle`):** bỏ `prepare` khỏi lifecycle tự động trong `package.json`; thêm `scripts.setup:hooks` (cùng lệnh) làm việc dev thủ công chạy 1 lần sau khi clone; thêm test chống-hồi-quy khẳng định `package.json` không còn `prepare` — loại bỏ hẳn trigger cho MỌI package manager, không riêng pnpm. Trade-off: contributor phải tự nhớ chạy lệnh setup 1 lần sau clone, đổi lại loại bỏ hoàn toàn friction cài đặt cho mọi người dùng cài qua git. Liên quan trực tiếp STR87 (cùng vùng install/setup) nhưng tách riêng vì đây là bug thật đang chặn cài đặt, cần fix độc lập, không chờ câu hỏi Rust-vs-Go của STR87. — done

### Playbook: verify-fail-post-merge

- **Signal**: `{picked: <id>, approve: {blocked, reason: "verify-fail-post-merge"}}` — the post-merge verify genuinely ran and failed (`timedOut` is absent or `false`); the merge was rolled back and the target is unchanged.
- **What the machine tries**: Walk `docs/how-to/diagnose-a-verify-fail-post-merge-block-on-approve.md`'s steps directly, in this same session:
  1. Read `approve`'s own `output` field from the response (the full test-suite output, not just the recorded `verify` command) and identify exactly which test(s) failed.
  2. Check whether the failing test's file is inside the item's own diff (`fgos review <id>` or branch's changed files) — a failure in a file the item never touched is the first signal it's unrelated noise.
  3. Re-run the failing test file alone a few times (`node --test path/to/the-failing.test.mjs`) — reproduces deterministically (a genuine pre-existing bug) or only fails under full-suite run (load-induced flake).

The driver must never accept worker self-narration, conversational claims, or ungrounded status reports:

2. **Verify Clean Tree:** Verify `git -C "$wt" status --porcelain` is clean (all worker edits committed).

# The pane is attached under this session's key (idempotent when /fgOS:terminal
# already did it). Naming it as the caller's own pane is what lets the port
# close an attached pane: the one case where it does.
key=$(fgos_terminal_key "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-}")
fgos_terminal_attach "$key" "$HERDR_PANE_ID" || exit 0
fgos_terminal_call release "{\"key\":$(fgos_json_str "$key"),\"disposition\":\"close\",\"callerPane\":$(fgos_json_str "$HERDR_PANE_ID")}" >/dev/null || true
exit 0
